title: Sequential Function Chart (SFC) -- a Batch Sequencer
concept:
An SFC is steps + transitions: each STEP runs actions, and you advance to the
next step ONLY when its TRANSITION condition becomes TRUE. (Lesson 5 advanced
every scan; a real sequencer gates each move.) In ST you hand-code an SFC as a
guarded CASE state machine:

    CASE Step OF
        1: Valve := TRUE;
           IF Level_Full THEN Valve := FALSE; Step := 2; END_IF;  (* transition *)
        ...
    END_CASE;

Each step energizes its own output and moves on only when its condition is met.
ab_note: Studio 5000 has native SFC as a language; when you write it in ST, the guarded-CASE pattern is the standard hand-coded equivalent.
siemens_note: Siemens GRAPH is their SFC editor; in SCL you use the same CASE + IF-transition pattern shown here.
task:
Batch sequencer with Step : INT (0=Idle,1=Fill,2=Heat,3=Drain).
Inputs: Start, Level_Full, Temp_OK, Level_Empty : BOOL.
Outputs: Fill_Valve, Heater, Drain_Valve : BOOL.

  0 Idle : all outputs OFF; go to 1 when Start
  1 Fill : Fill_Valve ON; go to 2 when Level_Full (turn Fill_Valve off)
  2 Heat : Heater ON; go to 3 when Temp_OK (turn Heater off)
  3 Drain: Drain_Valve ON; go to 0 when Level_Empty (turn Drain_Valve off)

Use CASE Step OF ... END_CASE; with an IF transition in each step.
starter:
(* Lesson 15 -- Sequential Function Chart (SFC): a Batch Sequencer *)

VAR
    Step        : INT;   (* current SFC step, 0..3                    *)
    Start       : BOOL;  (* N.O. start PB -> XIC (as-is)              *)
    Level_Full  : BOOL;  (* hi-level float -> XIC (as-is): TRUE=full  *)
    Temp_OK     : BOOL;  (* thermostat    -> XIC (as-is): TRUE=at temp*)
    Level_Empty : BOOL;  (* lo-level float -> XIC (as-is): TRUE=empty *)
    Fill_Valve  : BOOL;  (* output *)
    Heater      : BOOL;  (* output *)
    Drain_Valve : BOOL;  (* output *)
END_VAR

checks.message: Executed: advances only when each transition condition is TRUE
checks.hint: A transition fires the scan its condition is TRUE; the new step's action runs the NEXT scan (one-scan entry lag).
